newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast spot products steady with mixed NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast spot products steady with mixed NYMEX.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast products were little changed Wednesday, as futures markets lacked momentum and gasoline stocks remained ample, leaving traders without a sense of the market's direction.
Crude oil for June delivery, which settled 14 cents a barrel to $19.73, contrasted with a 0.03-cent-a-gallon fall in unleaded gasoline futures.
A majority of today's deals were struck in the paper market, a place where refiners gamble on the direction of product prices without trading actual barrels.
Several hundred thousand barrels traded on paper, refinery traders said Wednesday.
April/May prices for ultra-clean CARB gasoline were unchanged at 70/71 cents a gallon, while San Francisco CARB was pegged 1.50 cents less.
Conventional unleaded gasoline for prompt delivery stood 66/67 cents, notionally steady with San Francisco at the same price.
Distillates eased Wednesday, with buyers of low sulphur diesel willing to pay 58 cents a gallon, a one cent drop from Tuesday.

Traders also yawned at the American Petroleum Institute's report late Tuesday of a 578,000-barrel-build in West Coast gasoline stocks that left inventories in the PADD 5 region at 26.7 million last week.
